Hey [~accountid:5d2899bcea26c40c204434af] 

Thank you for the comment and your idea sounds very logical. But in UA Rides, drivers cannot top-up their balance:

* We have an international payment set up, meaning that money from riders in Ukraine goes to Estonia via acquiring, Bolt calculates the drivers' balance, and the payout is made back to Ukraine.
* No possibility for users (both drivers and riders) to make payments out of Ukraine by SWIFT or similar systems - because of National Bank restrictions. We still have war in Ukraine and the government is trying to control the transactions to avoid massive outflow of funds. So banks will not execute such payments.
* We don't use Bolt Balance to collect money from users - as it’s a legal opinion that we need special financial license for operating digital money.
* Localization or any other fundamental changes to the payment setup are considered in the future but not earlier than next year due to the complexity of tax and regulatory risks. 

As a result, only the way to cover the negative balance for the driver - is to make in-app rides which can be problematic if the driver is blocked for fraud or serious safety issues.

Hi [~accountid:5b7beae8d08e47445d6fd025] - I have discussed with the team and our conclusions are the following:

* The Road Traffic Act (which the user has referenced) does not require Bolt to share user information with the cyclist who is making this request.
* Since data privacy law requires us to protect the personal data of our users, we should wait for a formal request from the police before providing this information.

Could you therefore please take the following steps:

# Send the below response to the individual making the request.
# Monitor the ticket for 7 days and let me know if we receive any follow-ups. If not, then the ticket can be closed.

----

Dear Todd,

Thank you for your request.

At Bolt, we take the privacy and security of our users very seriously. We only engage in data sharing with third parties where we are satisfied that the requirements of our third party data sharing policy have been met. This means that the request for data must be lawful, necessary, proportionate, and limited to the specific purpose outlined in the request.

After carefully reviewing your request, we have determined that we cannot provide you with a copy of the personal data requested because disclosure would violate the rights and freedoms of third parties. Nevertheless, if Bolt receives a formal request for the same data from the police to whom you have reported this incident, then we will consider the same.

If you have any questions in this regard, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

[~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] I understand we completed the testing of dynamic commission. Will this feature be implemented or are we still only in test phase?

* *From a regulatory point of view*
** As we noted before, we can implement a dynamic commission (ie commission charged can be lower than 25% at times and higher in others), however in PT due to the TVDE Law Bolt’s commission *cannot be higher than 25% on* +*each trip*+*.* Therefore, averages per week would arguably not be in accordance with the TVDE. 
** TVDE law also determines the following obligations in relation to commission:
*** “make +available to the user+ in a clear, understandable and objective manner, before the start of each journey and during it: a) The price calculation formula, indicating in particular the total price, the +intermediation fee applied+ and the applicable fares, namely by distance, time and dynamic fare factor;”
*** “after completion of the service provision, the electronic platform shall +send the user+ an electronic invoice, indicating, among other things: e) Demonstration of the price calculation, based on the elements and weighting factor that make up the respective calculation formula, including t+he intermediation fee charged by the electronic platform operator+.”
** Since these information requirements regarding commission are general to all the rides, regardless or not of the application of the dynamic commission, I suggest that we discuss this matter in the compliance project (in alignment with other support functions, namely tax [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] ) whether this actually applies to Bolt or not given the fact that Bolt is not the one providing the  transportation service. 
* *From a t&c point of view:*
** Dynamic commission is already foreseen in the current t&c: “8.6. Please note that the +Intermediation Fees chargeable may change from time to time, considering the principles of dynamic commission pricing+ that take into account (i) the balance of the supply and demand for the Transportation Service, (ii) characteristics of the ride ordered; and (iii) conditions of any applicable campaigns.” Hence no need to update t&c.
** We should discuss whether you aim to communicate this new feature or not to TVDE operators and how. I understand the commission would only decrease since we are already at the benchmark of 25% in PT. Nevertheless there is a general principle of communication in our t&c in 8.3 and I suggest that we discuss this point further to align (_“You acknowledge that the Intermediation Fee may change from time to time, but may not exceed 25% of the Trip Price (“Highest Rate of Intermediation Fees”), as defined in Article 15, paragraph 3, of Law No. 45/2018, of 10 August. Bolt undertakes to send You prior written notice of any changes.”_): can a driver see any info on the commission in the acceptance screen?

** The Supplier shall be liable for *all* personal injury or property damage caused by the Supplier or other legal or natural person for whom the Supplier is responsible, in the performance of the assignment, to the Region, the Passenger or other third party. The limitation of liability does not apply to the Supplier's obligation to compensate third parties or if the damage was caused by gross negligence or intent. {color:#ff5630}*This however means that the limitation of liability is uncapped regarding amounts which faces us with a risk of high costs for liability of damages. Hey [~accountid:712020:3c6c8d76-7a41-4491-a752-76e034e2c39a] Thanks for sharing. Interesting use case for Ride Booker, haven’t encountered before.

I’m aware of only one arrangement where such “ride request device” was introduced on 3rd party premises like hotels, i.e. [VenuButler |https://www.venuebutler.com/]but there it’s VB providing the devices which are placed so as far as Bolt is concerned it’s a fairly regular Ride Booker +API+ integration between us and VB based on our [RB API integration template|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3682600193/Ride+Booker+API.+Bolt+Business+Legal]. 

Here I understand it’s based on Ride Booker (not RB API). And it’s us providing the devices to the hotels (for receptionists and self-service for passengers). 

My first question would be +whether hotels are still required to have a Business account+ (which is typically a prerequisite for enabling the RB tool). _To determine the scope of contracting with hotels/passengers, also possible privacy considerations._ From the good notes you shared I believe hotels still need to sign up as our Business Customers for a Business account (e.g. considering the access/viewing rights of the hotel). _Hence I think we do not deem the rides requested using these devices to be requested independently by the passengers, leaving the hotels the role of “acquiring leads” or whatnot._

If it requires a Business account we should use Bolt Business account special terms as a starting point and modify it as needed, e.g. in relation to using Bolt’s hardware, any fees due, payment specifics if any, perks for hotel admins/ prepaid cards[?], exclusivity, reporting specifics etc. _If Business account not needed then Business General T&C wouldn’t be applicable - so more flexibility with regards to drafting from one end but we’d have to cater for the missing boilerplate included in the General T&C._

We might want to confirm with business [slide 6|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1wLqd9dzRk6BhpGpRoJqZPxT7CaXm47gBXIu3FEwI7U0/edit#slide=id.g319f3911cf7_0_126] stands as is to ensure alignment on how this arrangement would actually look like.

Perhaps related to the above, it’s not clear to me what does it mean to “+have a permanently assigned address in its Ride Booker+, allowing them to order rides for guests via Bolt”. 

What’s also unclear is +how would the cost be added to the ride fare charged from the passenger+. Shall  the ride price be inflated so that it’s the driver who’d charge passenger the extra (and our regular Rides commission increases proportionally) or is the aim rather that Bolt would charge passenger directly?

However afaik charging any fees by Bolt directly to the passenger has not been greenlighted globally. There is a whole project ongoing for that, see [#fees-for-users-global|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C06KE9RGF8Q/p1732042272508579]. _Perhaps smth can be greenlighted for PL fast-track - suggest to confirm with relevant badgers Fernando Berzosa (Rides), Andrew Short (Business), Beatriz Leiva (Legal)._ If however the intention is to inflate ride fee in a way that it would still be charged entirely by the driver (not Bolt) then possibly we have no legal issues but doubt if it’s commercially viable considering the margin we intend to share with hotels.

With regards to +regulatory risks in PL from enabling customers the RB tool+ it should be low risk but we do know that likely we’re not entirely complying with certain obligations to provide pre-trip information to the client (see here[ for PL|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xjttm8l2ccznZM69lGeCcErfCYqouHbToKftRe-ceAY/edit#gid=0]). Closing this gap with RB is in works globally, see [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LEG-438].

It seems for the time being this particular use case is isolated to PL (and CZ?) but if any questions remain it might be smart to loop in the Global Programmes & Partnerships (Bolt Business) team to clear any specifics. 

Hope it helps a bit.

Cheers for now!

* Legal basis (a reference to a law that creates us the obligation to disclose personal data to the requestor), usually it’s procedural laws, such as Code of Criminal Procedure, Law on Police or other laws regulating the powers of law enforcement agencies or intelligence agencies.
* List of data that we need to disclose
* Description of the crime, or a confirmation that the data is proportionate and necessary for the investigation.

For [~accountid:605ee2ff630024006fee58bb] and Marko to discuss and resolve in a quick 2-3 hour meeting on 16th Thursday

*Findings:*

* The city is not changed - the driver needs a new account for a new city.
** In Ukraine, drivers can have several profiles for different cities. They need to create a new one for each city.
** In other markets, the current profile needs to be closed.
*** Some markets advise the driver to delete the profile and submit a new registration.
*** Other markets escalate to OPS so the current account is deleted and the new one is created manually.
* Escalation to OPS:
** Agents are waiting for an update from OPS to inform the driver (sometimes it takes several days)
** Some agents just give the driver a timeline (e.g. your request will be submitted in 1-3 days) and close the case
** OPS don’t reply to drivers, they give the ticket back to CS
* LT & EE: waiting until the driver downloads documents from driver portal (needed for tax declaration) is very time-consuming and doesn’t depend on the agent. Since it is a time-consuming task for a driver, they don’t rush (e.g. they say “I will get to this once I have more free time”), and the ticket is kept on-hold until the driver gets back. {color:#bf2600}*Do we have other options to give the driver their docs?*{color}
* Lots of general questions and lack of info for drivers: they don’t understand how city change works; how bonuses are added when working in different cities; how long the city change will take; why in LT and EE they need to download docs; etc. {color:#bf2600}*Review the FAQs and Alfred’s informative message to the drivers.*{color}



*Possible solutions*

* CS deletes the driver’s account and ask them to submit a new registration. OPS receives a new driver lead registration and registers them as they normally would.
** *Pros*: Quick process without escalations. 
** *Cons*: Possible additional tickets from the driver once they submit a new registration. TRT would reduce just for this issue tag, but in general the whole process might be even longer for the driver.



* CS takes over the process of registering new drivers. When driver wants to change a city, they delete the account and register the driver to a new city. 
** *Pros*: CS able to handle driver lead registrations & changing the city cases on their own, without escalating to OPS. A task took over from OPS.
** *Cons*: Unsure if OPS would agree, high possibility that not all markets would and we would end up with lots of market specifics. Increased workload for CS - unsure if CS would agree globally.

{quote}Data Protection regime we can justify sharing the data in accordance with:

* *S30(b)(iv)* of the Data Protection Act, 2019 - {{Lawful basis}}: the _performance of any task carried out by a public authority_; and
* *Regulation 56(b)* - {{Exemption}}: A permitted general situation referred to under regulation 55 (a) relates to the collection, use or disclosure by a data controller or data processor of personal data about data subject including for _taking appropriate action in relation to suspected unlawful activity or serious misconduct._

I cannot find a specific legal basis that the Police can rely upon to request the data, but this doesn't mean there isn't  any event, provided that we can justify our sharing of the personal data, and that any sharing by us is *limited* to what is *absolutely necessary* for the police to perform their investigation/duties.{quote}

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore provide a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled, in particular information on the devices currently associated with your active Bolt account.

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

To reiterate - after a thorough review, we confirm that our teams found no evidence of personal data misuse or any incidents involving your personal data. However, if you have any additional questions or concerns, in this regard, please let us know.

Hey [~accountid:6295bc739582b8006fc4879b] 

Can you confirm if the proposed feature will function exactly as described in April 2024—i.e., if a driver rejects 5 trips while in the dispatch area, they are moved to the back of the queue? If so, the risks previously raised by Legal remain unchanged:

# *Freedom to Accept or Decline Trips:* I’d like to highlight clause 16.1 of the driver terms, which states:
_"When a Driver receives an offer from Bolt UK to fulfil a Journey in the Driver App, the Driver may elect to fulfil the Journey or decline the offer."_  This feature contradicts this clause, as it penalises rejections.
# *Control Concerns:* Using driver data to penalise rejections could be seen as exerting control, control mechanisms align more with a worker status than an independent contractor model, an issue raised during the employment tribunal proceedings and noted in the judgment.

While I understand the feature’s benefits, improving acceptance rates, airport wait times, and passenger experience these should be we weighed against the risks. The business is currently maintaining an independent contractor model in the UK, introducing features that disadvantage drivers could undermine this position. I would assess this feature as {color:#ff991f}*moderate risk*{color}, but similar features cumulatively elevate the risk to {color:#bf2600}*high*{color}. Similar to my advice on dynamic commission, while FIFO alone may not trigger reclassification, combined with other factors, it could increase the likelihood of an Employment Tribunal ruling against Bolt. 

Additionally, this feature falls into the category of ‘*rider-driver matching and dispatching’*, where Privacy Legal ([~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] / [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] ) has advised pausing rollouts. This includes features related to:

* Rider-driver matching and dispatching
* Fraud prevention
* Price setting and safety

[~accountid:6295bc739582b8006fc4879b] [~accountid:5d8df399c7d4e30dc2836580] The business may proceed with FIFO if it fully understands and accepts the associated risks. However, as Bolt Services UK Limited has already been reclassified, further risks could weaken our defence of the independent contractor model. If the decision is made to move forward, I recommend postponing the rollout until the ICO investigation is resolved and Privacy Legal approves.

Any questions please feel free to reach out.

*** *Payout not processed*: AWX will inform us for Driver bank details to transfer the remaining money themselves. Hopp to  provide more info to AWX. We can then close the account, since AWX will send the money to the Driver, and immediately close their account too.

While I understand the business's position—that the driver voluntarily shared their information with the scammer, here are the reasons for my recommendation:

# If the driver claims against Bolt in small claims court, Bolt would likely have a weak defence. Since the incident occurred on the Bolt platform, a court may expect us to have safeguards in place to prevent such scams.
# Though Bolt provides communications and guidelines to drivers on handling scams, these are not in the form of mandatory training (as drivers are independent contractors we are not permitted to require mandatory training). Therefore, the driver could argue they didn't review these materials.
# Generally, the court would likely view the driver as being in a more vulnerable position compared to Bolt and may deem it unfair for the driver not to receive the fees owed.

This is ultimately a business decision, and I understand the reasons for withholding payment to the drivers affected by the scam. However, I would like to highlight that any defence we might raise in the event of formal legal proceedings being issued against Bolt would likely be weak. However, I appreciate that formal proceedings have not been initiated yet, therefore if you decide to proceed by not paying out the driver at this stage, if formal proceedings are issued the legal team can assist in the response. However, please note, the cost and resources involved in defending a claim of this nature would likely exceed the amount requested.

Query to retrieve needed entities: 

{noformat}with
company_invoicing_strategy as 
(
  select
  distinct company_id
  from etl_billing_invoicing_fee_calculator_daily
  where country_code = 'ro'
  and date = current_date - interval '1' day 
  and invoicing_strategy = 'company'
),
company_earnings as 
(
  select 
  'ride_hailing' as vertical,
  entity_company_id,
  sum(gmv_gross) as gmv_gross
--  max(period_date) as last_ride_date
  from etl_billing_entity_driver_activity e
  left join fleet_company fc on e.entity_company_id = fc.id 
  left join company_invoicing_strategy dis on dis.company_id = e.entity_company_id
  where period_date >= date '2024-12-01'
  and fc.country = 'ro'
  and dis.company_id is not null
--  and entity_id in (2212383, 1414878)
  group by 1,2
),
courier_fleet_earnings as 
(
  select 
  'delivery_courier' as vertical,
  entity_id,
  entity_company_id,
  sum(gmv) as gmv_gross
  from etl_billing_entity_courier_activity e
  left join ng_delivery_spark.dim_courier dc on e.entity_id = dc.courier_id
  left join admin_system_city sc on sc.id = dc.city_id
  where period_date >= date '2024-12-01'
  and sc.country_code = 'ro'
  group by 1,2,3
)
select distinct e.entity_id, e.entity_type, e.address
from etl_billing_tax_all_entities e
left join company_earnings fe on e.entity_id = fe.entity_company_id and e.entity_type = 'fleet'
left join courier_fleet_earnings cfe on e.entity_id = cfe.entity_company_id and e.entity_type = 'courier_fleet' 
where country = 'ro'
and e.admin_status = 'active'
and coalesce(fe.gmv_gross,cfe.gmv_gross) > 0
order by e.entity_id desc{noformat}

Therefore, unless a relevant solution is agreed with Solid, in my opinion keeping the agreements in force is unreasonable (the INS agreement was not performed and without prior performing INS Agreement, the SGN Agreement cannot be performed - the agreements are related). 

The INS Agreement (sale and installation of detectors) does not regulate the possibility of termination in case of non-performance of the agreement due to reasons attributable to the Contractor, therefore respective provisions of Civil Code shall apply. In principle, *we can terminate the agreement at any time* and in this case also for a valid reason - the agreement was not performed in due time. *As for the advance payment - generally it is fully refundable*. 

If the INS Agreement will be terminated, the SGN Agreement shall also be terminated at the same time, as it will be not possible to perform the SGN Agreement. 

Provisions relating to the termination of the agreements:

+*SGN Agreement:*+

_§ 6.1.b - agreement can be terminated by any Party with 3 months' notice period,_ *_unless the Parties agree otherwise_*_. [_{color:#36b37e}_Legal: the agreement should be terminated at the same time as the INS Agreement_{color}_]_

_§ 6.4 - If the Contractor does not undertake the execution of the concluded Agreement or the related INS agreement and the Contractor does not receive the Facility Report Card within 12 months from the date of signing of this Agreement, the Agreement shall automatically terminate as not performed._ 

+*INS Agreement:*+

_2.4 The order to install the system shall be executed by the Contractor within 7-15 business days from the date of the Contractor's account being credited with the amount due as an advance payment towards the performance of this Agreement. [_{color:#36b37e}_Legal: I understand that the installation was not commenced_{color}_]_

+*BACKGROUND:*+

* In September 2024, the driver’s [account|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/870367?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] was hacked as a result of OTP phishing (see [+LSS-39367+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-39367]). 
** Driver suffered financial detriment as a result of the hack (Driver's balance before compromise was £476.02, which was then brought into negative balance by suspicious payouts. Also, £1,111.77 of earnings not paid out as a result).
** Driver’s account was not blocked until two days after reporting the incident to CS.
** CS assisted driver with restoring account access. Also, negative balance brought to zero.
* After completing review of the incident, we notified the user of a personal data breach on this [ticket|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/503266688] on 10 January 2025.
* Driver responded on the same day with the following:
** (1) “_from where or how the hacker managed to obtain my personal details?_”
** (2) “_As you may able to see from the data sheet that my hard earned weekly was gone on 16 September 204 to hackers account. Now my question is why Bold failed to stop the payment going through? Bolt had two days to act, and during these two days I urged bold to stop the payment going to the hacker account. I made phone calls and sent messages through app. But unfortunately my concerns wasn’t taken seriously by bolt_”
** (3) “_why bolt punishing drivers and treating us unfairly by not paying our hard earned cash_”
** (4) “_why Bolt app is not fit for purpose and place or put strict safety regulations standard to safe guard such breach of drivers personal details_”
** (5) “_why bold is not paying my hard earned cash for that particular week. After all Bolt admitted on the day my bold account was hacked. I therefore, kindly request that bold pay the amount which owe me_”
** (6) “_lately it came to my attention that on the day my bold account was hacked, I had four French passengers, three male one female. I picked them from W11 area and dropped them at Camden High street, near Mornington Station. When I dropped them their destination, soon I had another order near Euston Station, Eversholt Street. As I was driving towards to the pick up, the last passenger ( the four French nationals) who I already dropped called me, to say they left a bag in the vehicle and asking to return. By chance, my order which I was going to pick was cancelled. I told to the last passenger, I would return as my current order was cancelled. So I returned to the last location and they took the bag from the vehicle . The reason I stated this long episode is that, as in my opinion, these four passengers deliberately left an item in the car. This is because to try and test Bolt telephone line. Furthermore, the hacker who called me a couple of hours later through Bold app had also similar French accent. Bolt can find that passenger account and monitor its activity. This my own assumption, I could be right or wrong_”
** (7) “_once again I am stating that the hacker called me through bolt app, not my own mobile phone number. I therefore, my account was hacked through Bolt app. This means the safety and security data of likes of me drivers were breached. Instead of Bold compensate my loss of hard earned cash income, Bolt blocked me for a while and refused to pay me a week from 9 September to 15 September 2024_”
* Driver is demanding their overdue payout.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Responses to points raised:
** (1) *This is a Privacy point.* We have already partly explained this to the user (“_Individuals falsely holding themselves out to be other drivers, riders, and members of the Bolt Support Team may have asked for information from you to gain access to your account_”).
*** In particular, we know from [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/439047034] that on 13 September someone called the driver claiming to be from Bolt, and asked them for their personal details including an activation / OTP code. This is how the scammer gained access. IMO we should not respond in detail on this point, but re-hash what we have already said.
** (2) Loop in Ops for some language to prepare here.
** (3) There is not really a point to respond to here.
** (4) *This is a Privacy point.* We have already explained to the user the steps we have taken, as well as a general overview of our commitment to security. IMO we should not respond in detail on this point, but re-hash what we have already said.
** (5) As with point 2, this is something for Ops.
** (6) This seems to be based purely on speculation. We can respond at a high level saying that Bolt is continuing to monitor suspicious accounts and deal with them accordingly.
** (7) This is addressed with the other points above.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Ops should resolve the payout issue per the new approach of reimbursing drivers.
* Ops should also prepare some language re the delay in bank account blockage.
* Once the above have been actioned, Ops should contribute to the below response and we can send it to the user. [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] FYI - I am keeping our response high level here as I think it would be better to avoid over-sharing.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 20 November 2024, Lithuanian rider recognised an unrecognised charge on their Bolt account. Rider wanted a refund for this.
** Rider then complained to Bolt CS about various trips they did not recognise (e.g., on 21 Nov, they saw charges of [€4.80|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/1798590769/251?orderTryId=2131224640] and [€3.90|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/1798234036/251?orderTryId=2130767840] for trips they did not make). Bolt CS investigated and apparently the trips came from the user’s account.
** Rider then subsequently flagged that the phone number on the account was not theirs.
* Based on internal investigation by CS at the time, there were “_no new logins, nothing that would indicate a compromised account_”. As a result, account was never blocked.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Based on my own internal investigation:
** No account detail changes at the time of the unrecognised charges, and no logins from new devices. This suggests that this is unlikely to be a case of phishing.
** The trips at issue were taken from the user’s account. This suggests this is not a case of another user accidentally using the same personal details on their own account.
** If the phone number on the account is not the rider’s then it is not fully clear to me how exactly the rider themselves has access to the account. As such, this +*_could_*+ be a recycled phone number issue.
* Financial loss here seems to be very minimal. IMO unlikely to be reportable, particularly if we can resolve this.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] I will ask some follow-up questions to dig into this a bit more. Per the above, it is unclear to me what has happened here, but the only thing I can think of is phone number recycling. Let’s see what CS has to say.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 24 November 2024, Lithuanian rider wrote to Bolt CS concerned that someone had hacked their account. 
** The rider asked how they could delete their card details. AIFred responded that they should contact their bank and cancel the card. User cancelled their card on the same day.
** Later that day, the rider noted “_I'm all sorted now, thank you_… _The phone number that appears next to my profile is mine. I have not added a new device or shared personal information… someone is currently using my account and has messaged me to clarify_”. *However*, they  later wrote “_This message was written by another person who uses my account. Today I saw that my bank has been debited with the bolt, even though I didn't go anywhere myself_”. As such, it appears that Bolt CS were messaging an unauthorised third party, who was pretending that there was no issue.
** User noted that the unauthorised third party was making most of the unauthorised trip to or from the address ‘draugystės gatvė 9B’. They sent screenshots of the same from their Bolt app.
** User notes that mixture of card and cash payments were used to pay for the unauthorised trips. 
* All unrecognised devices were logged out by CS in response.
* User has since regularly asked for updates, but not been provided with any.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Based on my own investigation:
** On 24 November 2024, there was a login from a device other than the user’s phone 
*** Method: *cross-app*
Parent session ID: *458195673*
IP: 90.131.32.251
Kaunas, Lithuania
14 Sept 2024, 13:10 (UTC+03:00)
** No changes to the account details took place around the time of possible compromise.
** Devices were logged out, so it appears that the issue is not ongoing.
* Thoughts:
** Seems unlikely to be a case of phishing. We have not seen anything to suggest that the user shared their account information, and none of the account details were changed.
** Since it seems we messaged an unauthorised third party through the user’s account, it is also unlikely that this is a case of another user having similarly account details.
** It also seems unlikely that this is a case of phone number recycling, as the user appears to still have access to their app.
* Next steps:
** Dig into what this ‘cross-app’ access could mean.

{quote}Bolt does not offer personalized discounts based on app activity and previous orders, correct?{quote}

this is incorrect, or at least open for interpretation.
we have pretty sophisticated targeting based on various parameters, some of which can be interpreted as personalisation:

* user lifecycle campaigns (one discount for a new user, another for a frequent user, third for churned users etc.)
* having consumed a specific campaign (most campaigns are limited in nr. of uses, so one user can have consumed it, another did not)

and so on.But aside of that there are multiple other things that can influence:

* ab-testing — just randomly selecting users to enjoy a discount (usually about 90% of the whole population)
* location — we might give a discount in one city zone, and do not give it in another
* hiccups service stability (Incentives component did not respond in time)

etc.from the screenshot it’s very clear that the users are in different stages of their lifecycle for this restaurant, as on the left screenshot you see “Order again” category, and on the right it’s missing.
It means that the user on the left has placed an order from this restaurant within last year.

*_Data to be processed:_* amount of hours the driver was online

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Article 22 ssessment*
{panel}

*Is the processing automated?*

The described process involves collecting data on the amount of time a driver is online. If the time exceeds 10 hours, the driver is automatically and temporarily suspended. After 10 hours following suspension, the driver is unblocked. This action is undertaken in compliance with Portuguese law.

The suspension is solely automated and does not involve human intervention in determining whether the driver should be suspended or unblocked.

*Does it produce legal or significant effects?*

* The suspension is temporary and governed by a fixed threshold (10 hours of activity), with reinstatement occurring automatically after another 10 hours.
* While the suspension may inconvenience the driver, its impact does not appear to significantly affect them in a substantial manner or produce legal effects. For instance, it does not permanently affect their employment status, earnings, or legal rights.

*Does it fall under any exceptions under Article 22?*

Yes, this falls under the exception set in Article 22(2)(b).

* The process is implemented in compliance with *Portuguese law*, which mandates limits on working hours for drivers. This legal obligation under Article 6(1)(c) of GDPR provides a lawful basis for processing.
* Even if this were considered ADM, Article 22(2)(b) provides an exception for ADM that is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation, which applies here.

h4. Conclusion:

:green_circle: This process *does not fall within the scope of Article 22 GDPR* for the following reasons:

* While the suspension is automated, its *impact on the individual is not significant* enough to trigger Article 22.
* The decision is *necessitated by compliance with Portuguese law*, providing a lawful basis for the automation.

The PDPPL does not have applications outside Qatar - it only applies to *data controllers* located in Qatar. 

The QFC Law (regulates the Qatar Financial Centre) rules apply to the processing of personal data by a data controller/processor incorporated or registered in the QFC. Also, the rules of QFC apply to controllers and processors that are not incorporated in the QFC, *if* they are processing personal data as part of ongoing arrangements for data controllers/processors incorporated in the QFC. 

*This will therefore bring third-party contractors and related companies within the scope of the QFC's Data Protection Office supervision.* - [~accountid:5d43ea3f1a6bf10be6db0f6e] to check this further: PDPPL does not apply to us, as Bolt Operations OÜ is not located in Qatar, and it will be launched as a partner market. Therefore, the partner is responsible for ensuring they are compliant with the local law. However, we need to check if there are any registration requirements for Bolt Operations OÜ coming from the QFC Law and rules. 

*If only the QFC Law and rules apply to us*, we (Bolt Operations OÜ) are required to:

* Maintain written records of all processing activities
* Carry out a DPIA *only* for high risk activities. There is no explanation of what would be considered as high risk. In general, DPIA must be carried out in case of:
** ADM, incl profiling with a legal effect/if it significantly affects the DS
** processing sensitive personal data on a large scale
** systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale

There is no requirement to appoint a DPO.

The biggest problem with graphic displays is that we dont have proper prior experience with them. There are a lot of unknown unknowns that we learn about during the process of speccing and communication with the potential suppliers. 

Since the requirement is clearly visible display under direct sunlight and during night time we must select either 

* Transflective TFT
* or High brightness (800+ , ideally 1000+ nits) IPS 

Currently we have only one potential part for the high brigthness IPS panel which we have ordered sample and a demokit. Its price is 4.9 USD at 5k units. Transflective TFTs are roughly 2x more expensive. We can consider that ca 5 USD is the average price for 2.8” IPS. There might be cheaper ones if we have more time to look for the suppliers.

In addition to the display itself we need following components that drive the bom cost:

* a spearate MCU - 1.9 USD
* code memory for the MCU - 0.2 USD
* Storage memory for MCU - 0.64 USD
* ribbon cable connector for the display - 0.45 USD
* additional power circuits - 0.8 USD

in total this adds up to: *8.99 USD*



Big headache is the time diference between CN and EE and also the lack of technical knowledge of the procurement team in this field, which leads to lots of delays. Since we have huge time pressure, we might not have time to properly select the best display. Currently the (only) selected display seems OK, but it is still a gamble - we must physically test it in the real plastics to see its performance under direct sunlight. 

As I mentioned there are lots of unkown unkowns, we might get into some trouble during the testing and development and this might lag the timeline.

{noformat}WITH paytopay AS
(
	SELECT 
	x.*,
	CASE WHEN LAG(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS prev_is_null,
	CASE WHEN LEAD(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS next_is_null,
	LAG(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_id,
	LAG(x.crt) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_created,
	LAG(x."method") OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS prev_method,
	LEAD(x.id) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_id,
	LEAD(x.crt) OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_created,
	LEAD(x."method") OVER(PARTITION BY x.client_id ORDER BY x.crt ASC) AS next_method
	FROM (
			SELECT
			pp.client_id,
			pc.external_id AS driver_id,
			pp.id,
			date_trunc('day',pp.created) AS crt,
			pp."type",
			pp.target_amount,
			pp.target_currency,
			pp."method",
			pp.state,
			pp.created_date
			FROM glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_payout AS pp
			JOIN glue.ng_payout.invoicing_payment_client AS pc ON pp.client_id = pc.id
				WHERE pp."method" = 'regular'
				AND pp."type" = 'ride_hailing_driver'
				AND pp.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
	) AS x 
		WHERE x.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
		ORDER BY x.crt DESC
),
checks AS 
(
	SELECT 
	p.calculation_id,
	p.payout_id,
	p.calculation_date,
	p.driver_id,
	p.country,
	p.decision,
	p.payout_amount,
	p.currency,
	p.payout_amount_eur,
	p.rule_name_array,
	s.strat,
	p.created_hour
	FROM ng_public.etl_driver_recurring_payout_check AS p
	CROSS JOIN UNNEST (p.rule_name_array) AS s (strat)
	WHERE p.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
),
flags AS 
(
SELECT 
foc.city_id,
foc.order_id,
foc.user_id,
array_agg(facr."type") AS flags_array,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr.is_fraud IS NOT NULL THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_flags,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" LIKE 'REPETITIVE%' OR facr."type" LIKE 'SAME%' THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_repetitive_or_self_flags,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" LIKE 'REPETITIVE%' THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_repetitive,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" LIKE 'SAME%' THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_self,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" IN ('DRIVER_DID_NOT_PICK_UP_RIDER','RIDE_DID_NOT_HAPPEN') THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_intrerrupted_ride
FROM ng_public.fraud_order_check as foc 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as facr ON facr.order_check_id=foc.id AND date(facr.created_date) >= DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date)
WHERE foc.created >= DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date)
AND foc.created_date >= DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3
)
SELECT 
ptp.crt,
ptp.id,
ptp.state,
cc.*,
co.order_id, 
co.city_id, 
co.country_code,
co.created, 
co.driver_courier_id, 
co.payment_method_type, 
CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type = 'default' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cash_trip,
CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type = 'business' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS business_trip,
CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type <> 'business' AND co.payment_method_type <> 'default' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS inapp_trip,
co.partner_price,
co.user_price,
co.user_price_eur,
co.partner_price_eur,
co.partner_price_eur - co.user_price_eur AS covered_by_promo,
CASE WHEN (co.partner_price_eur - co.user_price_eur) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS rider_campaign_order,
co.refund_amount,
co.refund_amount / co.eur_currency_rate  AS refund_eur,
co.fraud_refund,
co.is_final_failed_payment,
co.is_chargeback,
co.is_payment_problem,
co.propagated_chargeback,
co.reporting_fraud_loss_eur,
co.potential_fraud_loss_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS chargedback,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS failed_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS problem_payment,
CASE WHEN (co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS pay_issue,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_payment_problem = TRUE OR ff.count_flags > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS trip_issue,
CASE WHEN ff.count_flags > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_fraud_flags,
CASE WHEN ff.count_repetitive > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_fraud_flags_repetitive,
CASE WHEN ff.count_self > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_fraud_flags_self,
CASE WHEN ff.count_intrerrupted_ride > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_fraud_flags_RDNH,
ff.flags_array,
ff.count_flags
	FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
	LEFT JOIN flags ff ON ff.order_id = co.order_id AND ff.city_id = co.city_id AND ff.user_id = co.user_id
	JOIN paytopay AS ptp ON co.created < ptp.crt
							AND co.driver_courier_id = ptp.driver_id
							AND CASE WHEN 	
										ptp.prev_is_null = 0 THEN co.created > ptp.prev_created
										ELSE 
										co.created < ptp.crt 
										END
	JOIN checks cc ON cc.driver_id = co.driver_courier_id AND ptp.id = cc.payout_id
WHERE
co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date) AND co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
AND co.order_state = 'finished' AND co.order_type ='rides'
AND co.driver_courier_id = 6641556
ORDER BY co.created DESC{noformat}

*Driver Queue Optimisation* (DQO) is considered a ‘high impact feature’ that is likely to escalate reclassification risk in +*any*+ market. This is because when using driver queue optimisation, the historic driver performances are used to “prioritise” or “de-prioritise” a driver in the “dispatch queue”, which may have the effect that “poor performers” will have less access to work as a result of Bolt’s discretion. In other words, Bolt is reducing the ability to access work if the driver does not accept work.

As part of the feature:

* Bolt is performing an ongoing assessment of ‘driver quality’ using numerous data points.
* It is Bolt’s algorithms that have the effect of a driver being less likely to access work.

However, the driver queue optimisation feature is _slightly_ less risky than “acceptance rate blocking”. I note that acceptance rate blocking is deactivated in Nigeria, however it was deactivated for operational reasons in that there was a loss in supply. 

Nigeria has a low risk of reclassification as we received two judgments in 2024 confirming driver’s independent contractor status. 

Launch does not require reclassification committee approval as this is a low risk market. 

In regard to the terms and conditions and whether they need to be updated/amended, in terms of Nigerian regulations and laws, *Bolt is not required to disclose the specific parameters of its algorithm that determine how drivers receive orders*. However, Bolt may provide general information regarding how the process works however this does not need to be included in the terms.

Thanks [~accountid:5f771bde95fe8e0069684e9a] , all clear. In that case, I’m happy for us to proceed, I just want to make sure that the risks laid out below by me are clear.

To summarize what gaps/risks I’ve identified and what we’re risking if we go with the agreement as-is from a privacy POV:


*High risks:*

* High risk of non-compliance and disruption to data flows if transfer mechanisms are invalidated.
* Lack of a specific timeframe for breach notifications could result in regulatory penalties.
Limited ability to object to sub-processors increases risks of non-compliance and security breaches.

*Medium risks:*

* Retention period described as "reasonably necessary" creates uncertainty and risks of GDPR non-compliance.
*  Liability limits may not adequately cover data protection risks, exposing the Customer to significant financial exposure.

*Low risk:*

* Conditional assistance may lead to delays or disputes in meeting GDPR obligations.



Having said that, I believe we’re okay to proceed, as the service provider will receive limited data, and the risks, even if formally high under law, are not something that's likely to materialize.

* *Transparency*
** Supplementing GDPR privacy notices with a dedicated section on PWD-specific topics (e.g., algorithmic decision-making and human oversight) should suffice.
** The local law may require platforms to regularly submit statistical data to authorities (e.g., the Ministry of Labor) for monitoring and policy-making purposes.
* *Restrictions of processing*
** Whether additional national restrictions apply beyond the PWD would depend on the Czech PWD transposing legislation and on other applicable Czech laws (e.g., the Czech GDPR adaptation act, applicable labour laws, etc.). Currently, there is no clear indication of extra categories prohibited specifically under Czech law beyond the standard GDPR regime.

We were specifically approached by the State Security Service (SSA) in Latvia to discuss potential cooperation. We had two in-person meetings and decided to sign a cooperation agreement. This agreement will outline, among other things, the exchange of information, the data request process/form, and the scope of cooperation. We plan to add the data request form as an annex to the agreement. Currently, the agreement is being drafted by the SSA, and once they share it with me, we will review it together with the privacy team.

In the meantime, they are sending data requests as per the usual process. I have explained to them that to disclose data, we need legitimate grounds and purposes, and the request must comply with the minimization principle by being limited to what is necessary. SSA explained that, unlike ordinary police, their focus is on crime prevention rather than reacting to crimes already committed. Therefore, it is difficult for them to define in advance what specific data they need or what might be useful. They argue that it depends on the circumstances when a crime occurs. However, since their purpose is to prevent crimes from happening, any data could potentially be helpful.

Due to this uncertainty, lack of full clarity and special authorization of the SSA to ensure state security, they have special legal exceptions allowing them to make information requests outside of the standard GDPR process  
Also, LV laws give them this right.  Specifically, the Law on State Security Institutions section 19(1)(1) provides that an official of a State security institution has the right to: Within the scope of competence, request and receive information, documents, and other materials from State and local government authorities, economic operators, organizations, officials, and other persons, irrespective of restrictions on their use. Information, documents, and materials shall be issued in the requested form and free of charge.

Dear Iryna,

This is report regarding the developments today:

* Before GCCA meeting, we had an internal meeting to discuss the negotiation points and strategy. Later we also met Raul (Smartly’s lawyer) to find out what to expect from GCCA.
* At the meeting with GCCA we discussed all open issues and our suggested amendments. For the ease of reference, please see attached our comments added to the summary document that we circulated earlier in December.
* GCCA’s priority is to have a trade representative as soon as possible. They pushed to have it within a week, since Bolt had almost 6 months to appoint it. We explained that this is a new requirement that Bolt has not faced in any jurisdictions and Bolt needs time to assess legal and tax implications of such appointment. Bolt is working on several options and the decision should be made at upper managerial level that requires more time. GCCA suggested to officially request them additional 20 days. Upon your confirmation, we can send GCCA an official request to allocate us additional 20 days for appointing a trade representative.
* GCCA also noted that the easiest mechanism would be to appoint a local company as a trade representative. According to them, they had discussed this option with the tax authorities and they are sure that it would not cause any tax exposure.
* During the discussion we also noted that we intended to shortly solve the local representative issue by appointing a lawyer. However, we dropped this option, because GCCA considers that the local representative would be personally liable for any financial sanctions that may be imposed against Bolt. We noted that we could not find any legal grounds for imposing the personal liability for the individual acting under the Power of Attorney. GCCA’s representative responded with joking tone: “you may go to the court”. That implied that GCCA will follow their policy/approach even if they do not have legal grounds for personal liability of the local representative.
* GCCA also noted that Bolt is required to inform the customers regarding the T&C amendments one month before the amendments take effect. The notice to the customers should focus only on the amendments and should be understandable for the customers.

To mitigate the risk of financial sanctions against Smartly or the trade representative, we strongly suggest to amend the T&C and solve other issues indicated in the GCCA’s decision before or upon appointing the trade representative.

On a separate note, GCCA noted that they received a complaint from the customer against Foodly and they are about to commence the case. According to them, a customer did not receive the ordered food, but the request for reimbursement was rejected. 

Considering the latest developments, we propose to have a call tomorrow to discuss further steps. I’ll be available anytime after 11 pm.

Kind regards,

Giorgi

Hi [~accountid:61c07bf9a54af90069a42e2f] 
As we discussed on [Slack|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C08888J35QW] the current issue is that:

* our currency rates are now uploaded with a UTC timestamp on end-of-day (which is correct). The real picture for AUD-EUR for the different timestamps looks like
UTC timestamp                                                                                        /  relevant EET time  /  relevant CET time   /  rate
30.12.2024 23:59:59 _(displayed as rounded to 31.12.2024 00:00)_  /  31.12.2024 02:00   /  31.12.2024 01:00    /  0.597478640139
31.12.2024 23:59:59 _(displayed as rounded to 01.01.2025 00:00)_  /  01.01.2025 02:00    /  31.12.2024 01:00   /  0.597710767759
* All manual journals and trial balance use the correct end-of-day rate 0.597710767759 for the date 31.12.2024. 
* The report “Currency Rates as of Date” displays (visualises) the time based on the local time of the user. If I personally is located in Tallinn (the local time is set in the user profile) then the time I see and put in the prompt will be Estonian time.
So if you type "31.12.2024 23:59" into the prompt - it will take it as Estonian time 31.12.2024 23:59:00 EET (= 31.12.2024 21:59:00 UTC) and return the last available rate for that time, which is 30.12.2024 end-of-day UTC: 0.597478640139.
If someone in Warsaw enters "31.12.2024 23:59" - it will be taken as 31.12.2024 23:59:00 CET = 31.12.2024 22:59:00 UTC and will also return 0.597478640139.

Suggestion for Estonian employees: use the first day of the next month and 02:00 time (03:00 in summer) to get correct rates for the report "Currency rates as of date" (example: 01.01.2025 02:00 for the end-of-day rate 31.12.2024). 
Our team will try to figure out later if it's possible to create a report that asks for the UTC time not for local time.

Active restriction means the user has recently logged in via a new device and tried to change personal info (e.g. email/phone). The user has to wait 48 hours before they can make such changes (unless they contact CS who can verify them and remove the restriction earlier). 

The process for handling blocks for active restrictions is in the 🥡🥕 [Eater: My account was blocked|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019896139?country=global&language=en] in Step 4, but I’ve created a task to update these guidelines as well as add them to the account deletion article. {code:sql}select 
k.driver_id, 
COUNT(k.order_id)
from 
(



with block_action as 
(
SELECT DISTINCT da.driver_id AS driver_id, 
CASE WHEN da.ACTION = 'fleet_block_driver' THEN 'SCHEDULE_BLOCK' ELSE 'HARD_BLOCK' END AS block_type,
da.comment AS strategy,
da.created AS action_date,
da.finish_time AS block_finish_date,
DATE_DIFF('day', da.created,da.finish_time) AS days_difference,
DATE_DIFF('day', da.created,da.finish_time)/7 AS weeks_block_time,
CASE WHEN da.finish_time > NOW() THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS still_active_block,
json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.country') AS country
FROM ng_public.fraud_action_driver_action as da
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_fraud.driver_statistics_check_input as fci ON CAST(json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.driverId') AS bigint) = da.driver_id AND fci.created_date BETWEEN timestamp '2024-12-01' AND timestamp '2025-01-01'
WHERE da.created_date BETWEEN timestamp '2024-12-01' AND timestamp '2025-01-01'
AND da.status = 'success'
and CASE WHEN da.ACTION = 'fleet_block_driver' THEN 'SCHEDULE_BLOCK' ELSE 'HARD_BLOCK' end = 'HARD_BLOCK'
--AND da.driver_id = 5695843 
ORDER BY da.created DESC
)
select 
etl.order_id as order_id, 
etl.created, 
DATE(etl.created),
CASE WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 15 and extract(hour from etl.created) < 19 THEN 'Afternoon' 
WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 19 and extract(hour from etl.created) < 21 THEN 'Evening' 
WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 21 OR extract(hour from etl.created) < 01 THEN 'Night'
WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 01 and extract(hour from etl.created) < 06 THEN 'Overnight'
WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 06 and extract(hour from etl.created) < 09 THEN 'Morning'
WHEN extract(hour from etl.created) >= 09 and extract(hour from etl.created) < 15 THEN 'Mid-day'
ELSE NULL END AS time_of_day,
etl.country_code as country,
etl.driver_courier_id AS driver_id,
etl.driver_courier_fraud_label,
ba.action_date,
DATE_DIFF('day', etl.created, ba.action_date) AS blocking_timeframe
FROM 
ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
left join block_action as ba on ba.driver_id = etl.driver_courier_id
WHERE 
etl.created_date BETWEEN timestamp '2024-11-01' AND timestamp '2025-01-10'
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
--AND etl.country_code = 'fr'
and etl.driver_courier_id = 5695843
and DATE_DIFF('day', etl.created, ba.action_date) = 0 
order by etl.created desc 
--limit 999 

) as k 
group by 1
order by 2 desc 
--limit 99{code}

{quote}_Dynamic commission is already foreseen in the current t&c: “8.6. Please note that the_ +_Intermediation Fees chargeable may change from time to time, considering the principles of dynamic commission pricing_+ _that take into account (i) the balance of the supply and demand for the Transportation Service, (ii) characteristics of the ride ordered; and (iii) conditions of any applicable campaigns.” Hence no need to update t&c._{quote}

^^^ just FYI that wording comes from the time where ‘*commission netting*’ was known as ‘*dynamic commission*’. Here’s the modern terminology which I’ll use for the remainder of this post:

* *Commission netting*: when Bolt has promised the benefit of an incentive, Bolt provides the value of that incentive via a reduction in commission.
* *Dynamic commission*: the headline rate of commission that Bolt applies (prior to any commission netting) varies from time to time. 

As commission netting does not adversely affect drivers (in any obvious and meaningful way), it does not have the same transparency concerns as dynamic commission. We should be mindful that how Bolt sets its commission rates is probably going to be subject to ‘automated decision making’ disclosures under PWD.

This is a tricky subject and how Bolt deals with commission generally is one of the outstanding points earmarked to be resolved in the new template terms, although there will probably not be a ‘final answer' as the approach taken probably ought to vary on a per market basis. No solution is perfect but here’s some options, for consideration and comparison:

* If commission rates are universally flat in the market, it might make sense to include that specific fixed rate in the terms (subject to Bolt either agreeing or informing the drivers / fleets otherwise). This might not reflect market practices.
* If the commission rate varies on a trip by trip basis, then ideally the ‘per rate’ rate of commission would be made available in the app. However, I know that this is unpopular with business teams. 
* If commission varies per trip *_and_* the rate is not set out in the app on a per journey basis, we might be vulnerable to arguments that Bolt is not being transparent with commission (which creates reclassification and fin. reg. risk):
** One option would be to state the highest default headline rate of commission in the terms and confirm that this may be such lower amount that Bolt applies from time to time (which may be on a per trip basis). That way, Bolt can always say that it always made drivers / fleets aware of the highest rate of commission that applies. [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] has applied this approach in Germany ([~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] - please provide this for reference only). 
** ^^^ Local teams may not like this if Bolt is intending to charge a very high rate of commission (i.e. a rate that upsets drivers) but if so that begs the question why they think it’s appropriate to charge such a high rate in the first place.

In order to determine the best path, it’s worth being certain of how it’s intended to be presented in the app (and how commission is currently presented / dealt with), if you haven’t already done so. That way, you can better gauge the corresponding risk profile 👌

query to sum up all dispatched bonuses for campaign:


{code:sql}SELECT
	SUM(CAST(JSON_EXTRACT(b.earning, '$.amount') AS REAL)) AS amount
FROM
	ng_public.conditional_campaigns_bonus_calculation bc
JOIN ng_public.conditional_campaigns_bonus b
ON
	b.id = bc.bonus_id
JOIN ng_public.conditional_campaigns_condition c ON
	bc.condition_id = c.id
WHERE
	c.campaign_id IN (490375)
	AND b.state = 'dispatched'{code}

Internal notes for Debora regarding Carrefour comments on General Terms:

* Marketplace fee definition - ideally would keep, but ok to remove for Carrefour
* Minimum order Value and Small Order Fee - ok to amend so that those are agreed between the parties. 
* clause [2.2 comment|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-FFV49gxMfJk40EE9vKFeihfYoBskSxq8yCP6Bolky0/edit?disco=AAABbnF-Dw0] - cannot agree.  Bolt only offers the platform for restaurants/merchants (i.e Partners) and couriers, which Partners can use to conclude sales agreements and sell their goods to the customers and independent couriers (i.e service providers) can use to conclude delivery agreements in order to provide delivery services to their customers. It is up to Partners and couriers whether they want to conclude sales and delivery agreements or not and under which circumstances they do that.  By providing only the platform where Partners or couriers can offer their products or services independently Bolt is only in the role of agent for Partners and couriers and hence, is not party to the sales agreement nor to the delivery agreement. Since, it is up to Partner to decide whether they conclude the sales agreement with the customer for specific product and price which Partner has appointed independently on its web shop (i.e accept the order) and it is up to the courier to decide whether it concludes the delivery agreement with the customer for delivering specific order from point A to point B with the price customer is ready to pay and at the time suitable for the customer (i.e accept the delivery order), then sales and delivery agreements are not under Bolt’s control and hence, Bolt is no way party to either of the agreements nor can be liable for those agreements.
* [clause 2.3 comment|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-FFV49gxMfJk40EE9vKFeihfYoBskSxq8yCP6Bolky0/edit?disco=AAABbnF-DwQ] - not exactly sure what they mean due to Goofgle translate. But the answer is basically the same as for clause  2.2. If they ask what is the relationship between Bolt and delivery partner then it is similar as it is with restaurant partner - it is a business relationship. Although delivery partner is independent service provider then we still expect them to use our platform in accordance with the laws, industry standard and minimum quality and not interrupting platform work. If they don’t do that then bolt has a right t suspend their account use, terminate the contract with them or demand the damages. Regarding the delivery agreement then client has right of claim towards the delivery partner, not towards the merchant if it is clear that delivery partner has not fulfilled their part as they should. 
* clause 2.4 - proposed wording seems to be ok in general. As I understand they don't want to enable cash payments. 
* clause 4.2 - as I understand they don’t want to sell any alcohol, tobacco, frozen products, energy drinks since they have excluded them. If so then seems ok. 
* clause 4.3 - tbh I don't get their amendment here in the 1st sentence. They are fully responsible for fulfilling the order as it was submitted by the client and solely liable for the sales agreement. The fact that they amend this wording here doesn’t exclude their liability under the sales agreement nor under the local and EU laws + partner’s specific obligation is also reflected under Client T&Cs which cannot be changed only bc of one partner. Off if they have some specific concerns itht heir POS or stock systems which may often result in inaccurate stock levels and failings in orders then they should let us know about it and in this case probs some specific disclaimer should be added again under their profile on BF app. 
* clause 4.4 amendment on the last sentence - ideally I wouldn’t delete it but rather amend it and specify that if wrong order was picked-up due to Partner’s fault then Bolt has the right for deductions, burden of proof on them. It is probs linked to refunds policy so need to look those two together - who refunds what and under what circumstances. 
* clause 4.5 amendment on the last sentence - not quite sure how we can link obligations from this agreement to delivery partner T&Cs so I would leave that part out. However, if they insist of having e.g. additional disclaimer for courier related to delivery of some products, etc which can be implemented via courier app as “guidance” then this sentence also might be ok. Depends on what “obligations” regarding couriers CF wants to put on us. 
* 4.6.2 - we cannot delete due to EU regulations, such as EU Regulation 1169/2011, Regulation 2023/988, etc which all of them require merchant to provide product description and safety info before the purchase and obliges to provide product withdrawal and recall mechanism to consumers related to non-compliant products. See also MegaImage discussions [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C06EYG8FJ9Y/p1736429766210109?thread_ts=1736173804.827679&cid=C06EYG8FJ9Y]. 
* 4.6.4 - ok to amend. 
* 4.7 - didn’t get whether this was  for us or their internal note
* 4.8. ok to remove
* clause 4.9 - almost all their amendments, deletions are ok. Regarding 4.9.5 then example case is that courier goes to pick up the order on the time showed in the app and has to wait for the order for some X time due to Partner. Bc the waiting time has significantly exceeded for the client the client asks for Bolt to cancel the order since the waiting time has prolonged too much. In such case partner doesn't have to give over the order to the courier since order is cancelled due to partners prolong preparations. However, since courier is already at the partner’s establishment then courier still needs to be remunerated for the delivery fee. Since order was cancelled bc of the partner then that is why partner should cover the delivery fee. 
* 4.9.6 - probs should check over with the payment team
* 4.10 - 4.11 - seems ok to me. 
* 5.5 - what should be those guaranteed levels. What I would answer to them: As for any technology, Bolt cannot guarantee 100% fault-free operation of the Bolt Food platform in devices because quality of those devices as well as the use of those devices are not under Bolt’s control. For example, Bolt cannot check whether all relevant updates, programs, etc are done in some specific device which may affect the device and hence, Bolt Platform’s functioning in this device. However, as clause 5.5. refers then Bolt actually makes all reasonable efforts to keep platform running smoothly and for that Bolt provides updates, upgrades, modules etc occasionally to Partner which then Partner should implement since the device is under Partner’s control. Hence, we don’t see that this clause here should be concerning for the Partner. It is in accordance with industry’s best practice as well as real life situation. Thereat, we can assure that Bolt makes everything from its side to keep platform running smoothly for the Partner since it is also Bolt’s own interests that Partners can sell their goods on the platform continuously and customers buy them without any errors.
* 5.6. - why we should delete it. By using their own devices viruses risk is even higher. 
* 5.7 [comment|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-FFV49gxMfJk40EE9vKFeihfYoBskSxq8yCP6Bolky0/edit?disco=AAABbnF-Dwc] probs should check over with privacy, but DSA agreement should be part of the T&Cs and most probably covers this type of complaint handling is part of our operating model. They should check over the DSA. About removing the reference to specific complaint period then for now I would leave there 30 days but would let CF know that as a part of our global T&Cs update we plan to amend Partner T&Cs as well as client T&Cs and remove 30 days from there and lower it significantly - exact period is under the discussion. Since this 30 days period is also reflected currently on Client T&Cs then it should reflect for now also under the Partner’s T&Cs. 
* 5.9. - information society service in a simplified way is the platform service Bolt provides to partner to sell its goods. This clause basically means that Bolt has a right to shut down/end providing this service in whole or some parts of it (e.g. amend the app) if needed by notifyingg partner about it before. Quite logical tbh. 
* 5.11.1 - we have to notify them anw according to the Digital Services Act. So ok to add amendment. 
* 5.11.2 - cannot remove it. it is our right under the DSA. I think we have even discussed dit somewhere before and I shared relevant reference to DSA. What we can do is amend the wording and add that we can suspend etc those monetary payments if they are related to content which was illegal or contravened those T&Cs. 
* 5.12 - cannot delete. This is our right according to the T&Cs, it is related to our other obligations there. We also have those rights specified in our [complaint handling rules|https://bolt.eu/en-pl/legal/tnc-internal-rules/?category=delivery]. 
* 5.13 comments - see my comment for 5.9. 
* 5.1.4 - not sure why they think that Partners portal doesn't apply to them. Afaik they should add their menus etc via that. And, you should probs check it over together with Edik or Pawel. 
* 6.5 - tax consult needed.
* 6.6 - see marketplace fee part above.
